paper.title: ConTempo: A Unified Temporally Contrastive Framework for Temporal Relation Extraction
paper.code: Paper footnote 1 points to https://github.com/frankniujc/contempo (code + CleanMATRES). That URL returns 404 (checked 2026-09-26; Wayback captures of 2024-08-15 and 2024-08-16 are also 404; not in the author's 34 public repos). The paper's own input construction and CleanMATRES labels are therefore unavailable.

matres_annotations.format: docid, verb1, verb2, eiid1, eiid2, relation (TempEval-3 eiids)
matres_annotations.licence: No licence file or statement in the repository.

te3_platinum_text.note: TempEval-3 (UzZaman et al., SemEval 2013) annotated English test data, 20 .tml docs. The official te3-platinumstandard.tar.gz (cs.york.ac.uk/semeval-2013/task1) now returns 410 and has no Wayback capture; this copy is the one the MATRES README links to ("Update Jan 2022").
te3_platinum_text.licence: No licence stated by TempEval-3 or the copy; source texts are 2013 AP/CNN/NYT/WSJ news articles (copyrighted).

timebank_text.used: TBAQ-cleaned/TimeBank/*.tml for the 9 TB-Dense test docs (identical to the StructTempRel copy for these docs)
timebank_text.licence: TimeBank 1.2 is an LDC corpus (LDC2006T08); TempEval-3 redistributed the cleaned version without stating a licence. Source texts are 1998 news wire (copyrighted).

tbdense_annotations.note: Byte-identical to StructTempRel-EMNLP17/data/TempEval3/TimebankDense.full.txt. 12,715 relations over 36 docs (= Cassidy et al. 2014 Table 2). Codes: b, a, i, ii, s, v.

sentence_splitter.package: nltk==3.9.1 (uv run --with; not added to the project lockfile)
sentence_splitter.model: punkt_tab english, downloaded by nltk.download('punkt_tab') into data/raw/contempo/nltk_data; punkt_tab.zip sha256 e57f64187974277726a3417ca6f181ec5403676c717672eef6a748a7b20e0106; per-file hashes in data/frozen/contempo/raw_sha256.json

frozen.redistribution: Not redistributed: source texts are copyrighted news with no redistribution licence. Included in the repository: ID + SHA-256 per built row (data/frozen/contempo/{matres,tbdense}_test_ids.jsonl) and SHA-256 of every raw input file (data/frozen/contempo/raw_sha256.json). Rows are rebuilt into data/raw/contempo/built/ (gitignored) by `uv run --with nltk==3.9.1 python scripts/prepare_contempo.py`; `items()` refuses rows whose hash differs.
frozen.builder: scripts/prepare_contempo.py (--freeze writes manifests; default rebuilds and verifies)
frozen.row_fields: id, doc_id, event1, event2 (trigger text), context (sentence(s) with <e1>..</e1>, <e2>..</e2>), sentence_distance, gold

test_n_resolution.matres: 837 = all rows of MATRES GitHub platinum.txt (20 Platinum docs); ConTempo Appendix C: 'Ning et al. (2018b) released a version on GitHub that contains 837 relations in the Platinum test set ... We use Ning et al.'s (2018b)'. Label counts 424/269/31/113 equal the column totals of ConTempo Table 5 (BEFORE 424, AFTER 269, EQUAL 31, VAGUE 113). The Ning et al. 2019 preprocessed file (used by Relative Time code) also has 837 pairs but a slightly different label distribution (427/271/30/109); the GitHub version is used, as in the paper.
test_n_resolution.tbdense: 1,427 = event-event pairs of TimebankDense.full.txt in the 9 standard test docs whose two events both exist in TempEval-3 TBAQ-cleaned TimeBank. The full file has 1,785 E-E test pairs (8,130 E-E overall); 358 test pairs (2,042 overall) involve event IDs added only by TB-Dense annotators (e.g. e2078) and are excluded by the standard split: the remaining 6,088 E-E pairs are exactly the 6,088 E-E rows of rujunhan/TEDataProcessing TBDPairs.txt, and the 1,427 test (id, label) pairs are set-identical to its test-doc E-E rows. Train/dev/test 4,032/629/1,427 and test labels (VAGUE 638, BEFORE 384, AFTER 274, INCLUDES 56, IS_INCLUDED 53, SIMULTANEOUS 22) match Han et al. 2019's released test.pickle exactly.

input_construction.rule: Context = the sentences from the one containing the earlier event through the one containing the later event (MATRES and TB-Dense pairs lie in the same or adjacent sentences), whitespace-normalised, triggers wrapped in <e1>..</e1> / <e2>..</e2>. Event 1/2 order and gold direction as in the released annotation line. No DCT, no document beyond these sentences.
input_construction.why: ConTempo code unavailable. This is the standard sentence-level input of the baselines ConTempo reproduces (Ning et al. 2019 preprocessing used by Wen & Ji 2021 Relative Time; Han et al. 2019). The ConTempo unified framework additionally uses document-level GNN features and GPT-3 duration descriptions; Jev gets neither.
input_construction.sentence_split: TimeML TEXT split at line breaks, then NLTK Punkt within each line. Checked against Ning et al. 2019's MATRES preprocessing (wenhycs testset-temprel.xml, CogComp sentence splitter): all 837 pairs present; SENTDIFF agrees on 835/837; the 2 differences (nyt_20130321_cyprus ei10-ei13, ei10-ei15) come from Punkt splitting after 'G.D.P.', which only adds a sentence boundary inside an otherwise identical context. Same over-split after 'Sgt.' gives the 6 TB-Dense distance-2 pairs.

english_verification.metadata: TimeBank and TempEval-3 Platinum are English news (wire and broadcast transcripts); TempEval-3 separates English and Spanish tracks and these are the English files. The 4 APW test docs carry a LANG:ENGLISH wire profile; the CNN/NYT/PRI docs have no language field.
english_verification.method: All 2,264 built contexts checked: non-ASCII characters (0 contexts contain any); English function-word ratio per context (min 0.105); the lowest-ratio contexts inspected (all English, e.g. item CNN_20130322_1003:ei55:ei57).

metric.primary: micro-F1 over non-VAGUE labels (VAGUE predictions never count as true positives; VAGUE gold never counts toward recall). Paper Section 4.1 (p. 1527): 'The VAGUE labels are computed into the F1s for both MATRES and TBD but are regarded as negative labels.' Applied to both tasks. Implemented as sklearn f1_score(labels=non-VAGUE labels, average='micro').
metric.supplementary: accuracy (= micro-F1 with VAGUE as an ordinary class), macro-F1 over all labels, per-class F1, confusion matrix

paper_results.source: ConTempo Table 3 (p. 1528), F1 x100; ConTempo rows are means over 3 seeds; * = reproduced by the ConTempo authors under their evaluation settings

deviations: CleanMATRES (paper's re-annotated MATRES test labels, Table 3 first column) is not evaluated: it was to be released at github.com/frankniujc/contempo, which does not exist publicly. Only original MATRES and TB-Dense are scored.
Paper's exact input pipeline unknown (code not released); standard sentence-window input used instead (see input_construction).
TB-Dense SIMULTANEOUS is named EQUAL in ConTempo Table 1; label renamed only, same class (data code 's').
